 Judgment

Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 08.11.2011 passed by the Fast Track Court, Mangalore & Member, MACT, Mangalore D.K. (for short 'the Tribunal'), in MVC No.604/2008, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
That on 08.12.2007, the petitioner was proceeding in the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-19/V-747 as a pillion rider from Manipal towards Mangalore.

4. The Tribunal, based on the evidence let in, has awarded a compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- along with interest @ 6% p.a. under the following heads:-
Towards injury, pain, 1 50,000-00 suffering and mental agony Incidental charges which includes food, nourishment, 2 5,000-00 attendant charge and conveyance Loss of amenities and 3 25,000-00 enjoyment of life Towards diminution of 4 20,000-00 marriage prospects Total 1,00,000-00 5.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioner therein has preferred this appeal.
6. It is seen from the impugned order that the Tribunal has granted a meager sum of Rs.1,00,000/- to the petitioner.

The Tribunal has awarded the said amount on the ground that the petitioner sustained injuries to his face and that injuries has not come in the way of the petitioner from being physically fit and it would not come in the way of his future earnings.

It has also concluded that the petitioner subsequent to the accident has again met with an accident and the Doctor who has given his opinion about disability has been given subsequent to the second accident and thereby it is not reliable.
However, the injuries mentioned supra in paragraph No.3 is not in dispute.
The said injuries reveal apart from the fracture to mandible, he has lost 1/3rd of his tongue which has impaired his speech and he has lost 8 teeth, which is not in dispute.
This certainly leads to disfigurement of face and also impairs him from properly speaking.
The evidence also reveal that he was a second year B.Com student and his prospects for future earnings gets very much limited.
His marriage prospects are also dampened by this unfortunate incident.
It is seen that the petitioner was aged 20 years at the time of accident.
The treated Doctor has stated that he has a speech impairment of 25% and 21% disfigurement of the face.

Though the Doctor's opinion is based upon the examination of the petitioner after the second accident, the second accident does not reveal any injury to the tongue, it only reveals injury to the face.
So to award compensation towards 'loss of proper speech' has to be considered.
Given the Doctor's opinion, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has suffered the whole body disability at 9%.
The accident is of the year 2007 and if his notional income is taken at Rs.4,000/-, the petitioner would be entitled to a sum of Rs.77,760/- towards 'loss of future earnings' (4,000x18x12x9%).
Towards injury, pain, suffering and mental agony, given the nature of injuries, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/- and in my opinion it would be appropriate to enhance it to Rs.1,00,000/-.
With regard to medical expenses, it is submitted that the petitioner had medical insurance and the expenses has been reimbursed.
With regard to incidental expenses which includes food, nourishment, attendant charge and conveyance, a sum of Rs.5,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal.
In my opinion, it would be advisable to enhance it to Rs.10,000/-.
With regard to 'loss of amenities and enjoyment of life' a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal.
In my opinion, it would be just and fair to enhance it to Rs.50,000/-.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,37,760/-(Rs.3,37,760/- - Rs.1,00,000/-).

Hence, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is partly allowed;
ii) The total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified and petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,37,760/-(Rupees Two Lakhs Thirty Seven Thousand Seven Hundred and Sixty only) over and above what has been already awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition before the Tribunal till the date of realization subject to denial of interest for a period of 110 days.
iii) Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company shall pay the enhanced compensation to the petitioner along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of the judgment and order.
